name: Incline EZ-Bar Skull Crusher
description: The incline EZ-bar skull crusher is performed on an incline bench (typically 30-45 degrees), which shifts the angle of the arms relative to the torso. The incline position places even greater stretch on the tricep long head compared to flat skull crushers, as the shoulder angle changes the long head's initial length. This enhanced stretch stimulus at the bottom of the movement may improve hypertrophic adaptation in the long head.

execution.starting_position: Set an adjustable bench to 30-45 degrees. Lie back with the EZ-bar pressed to full extension above the face/forehead.
execution.setup_instructions: Have a spotter hand the bar off. The incline means the bar is above the face rather than above the chest.
steps: Step 1: Begin with EZ-bar extended above the face.
Step 2: Lower by bending only the elbows, bar traveling toward the forehead.
Step 3: Feel the stretch in the tricep long head at the bottom.
Step 4: Extend the elbows to press back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on press.
common_mistakes: Upper arms drifting on the incline
Using too heavy a load — the stretch position is more vulnerable
safety_considerations: The incline increases long head stretch — use lighter load than flat skull crushers until comfortable
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension to maximum elbow flexion with bar at forehead level.
coaching_cues: Feel the stretch at the bottom
